Anthony Albanese's government quietly grants permanent visas to 30,000 boat arrivals

Most of these people, which include over 6,500 people from Iran and over 4,500 people from Afghanistan, have already been living in Australia on temporary visas.

Actual Article Body:
By MAISY RAE - NEWS REPORTER

Published:  09:59 AEST, 28 September 2026   |  Updated:  12:11 AEST, 28 September 2026

165

View  comments

The Albanese government has quietly handed out permanent visas to more than 30,000 asylum seekers who arrived illegally by boat, sparking concerns that Australia's border security may be 'seriously weakened'.

More than 30,000 people who sought asylum by boat during the Rudd-Gillard era have now received Resolution of Status visas, The Australian reports.

Most of these people, including more than 6,500 from Iran and more than 4,500 from Afghanistan, had already been living in Australia on Temporary Protection visas and Safe Haven Enterprise visas.

Those visas, announced by then-immigration minister Andrew Giles in early 2023, were introduced to address the status of people who arrived during the surge in people-smuggling activity between 2009 and 2014.

The government had initially flagged that 19,000 visas would be handed out. However, the new total far exceeds that figure, with the publication calculating that visas were being issued at a rate of about 30 per business day.

It is understood that more than half were granted during the first 18 months of the visa program, with around 17,000 recipients having already become Australian citizens or becoming eligible to do so.

There was also a 22 per cent surge in the number of permanent visas granted to this cohort during the 2026 financial year.

The figure is backed by several immigration law practitioners quoted by The Australian, with one unnamed lawyer claiming permanent visas were frequently being issued before applicants could go to court.

More than 30,000 people who sought asylum via boats have now received permanent visas, according to reports

Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has been contacted for comment

'Very clearly, the government made a decision to issue these Resolution of Status visas to thousands of asylum seekers who were told they would never be resettled in Australia,' the lawyer said.

The Coalition's immigration spokesman, Jonno Duniam, said the increase in Resolution of Status visa grants represented a 'very serious weaking' of Operation Sovereign Borders.

'(It) bears out exactly what the Coalition has always said about the creation of this visa stream, especially that it would incentivise more people to be settled in Australia through this pathway,' Senator Duniam said.

'The Albanese government should never have dismantled the successful Temporary Protection and Safe Haven Enterprise visas, and they need to be urgently restored.

'Labor's claims that it would continue the former Coalition government's approach of ensuring that people who attempt an unauthorised boat journey to Australia will never settle permanently here are in tatters.'

According to the Department of Home Affairs website, permanent visa recipients are required to meet a number of requirements, including health, character and security criteria.

They must also sign and accept the 'Australian Values Statement', which calls for respect for the freedom and dignity of the individual, freedom of speech, commitment to the rule of law and a 'fair go' for all that embraces mutual respect and tolerance.

They must also commit to making 'reasonable efforts' to learn English if it is not their native language.

Permanent visa recipients must meet a number of requirements, including character and security conditions

A Home Affairs spokesperson said not all visa grants had been issued to people in the Temporary Protection visa or Safe Haven Enterprise visa cohort, and that some had been granted in response to recent humanitarian crises.
